name: Wakeio built-in source security regression corpus
description: Small, inspectable JavaScript and TypeScript fixtures for the public runSource API. Every input is synthetic and contains no real credential or customer data.
scope: The measured signal is the built-in AST candidate detector with tools: []. It is a scoped regression benchmark, not a production accuracy estimate.
unsupportedScope: Python semantics are outside this JS/TS AST corpus and are not represented as production coverage.
Real Next.js, React, Supabase, Express, database, or browser runtime behavior is not executed.
Network, package installation, authentication, and framework build behavior are outside the measurement.
Only the declared static local/relative-module subset is supported; dynamic dispatch, package imports and full framework reachability remain outside the model.
Koa ctx.request.query input is an explicit known miss in this corpus; other unrepresented frameworks and dispatch patterns are not covered by the measured denominator.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request query value is passed directly as the SQL argument.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request input remains connected to the SQL sink.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request value is interpolated into a statement variable before the database call.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request input remains connected through the statement variable.

cases.whyVulnerable: A query variable is reassigned from a safe literal to request input before execute.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; the reassigned statement reaches execute with request data.

cases.whyVulnerable: Request HTML is assigned directly to an innerHTML sink.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request HTML remains connected to innerHTML.

cases.whyVulnerable: Request HTML is first stored in a markup variable and then rendered.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request HTML remains connected through the markup variable.

cases.whyVulnerable: Request HTML is passed to insertAdjacentHTML.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request HTML is passed to the HTML insertion sink.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request command is passed directly to child_process.exec.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request command text reaches exec.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request command is copied into a variable before child_process.exec.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request command text reaches exec through a variable.

cases.whyVulnerable: A command is initially fixed but later reassigned from request input before execSync.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; reassignment replaces the fixed command with request input.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request URL controls the outbound fetch target.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request URL controls the outbound target.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request URL is stored in a target variable and passed to Axios.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request URL controls Axios through a variable.

cases.whyVulnerable: A request destination controls the Next redirect target.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; request destination reaches redirect directly.

cases.whyVulnerable: A destination variable is reassigned from request input before permanentRedirect.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; reassignment leaves request destination in the redirect argument.

cases.whyVulnerable: Request input crosses a helper function before reaching a database sink.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; the helper return still contains request data.

cases.whyVulnerable: Request input is built in one module and consumed by a sink in another module.
cases.whyFixed: No fixed variant is represented; the imported helper still builds SQL from request data.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would interpolate request data into the SQL string.
cases.whyFixed: The SQL structure is fixed and request input is a separate parameter value.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would pass request input as the statement argument.
cases.whyFixed: The database call receives only a static statement.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant is shown only in the comment and is not executed.
cases.whyFixed: The apparent request flow exists only in a comment; the executed statement is static.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would leave the tainted assignment as the final value.
cases.whyFixed: A tainted intermediate value is overwritten with a fixed statement before the sink.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would use an HTML parsing sink instead of textContent.
cases.whyFixed: Request content is assigned as textContent, which does not parse HTML.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would replace the literal with request HTML.
cases.whyFixed: The innerHTML value is a fixed literal.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant is present only as a string in this negative control.
cases.whyFixed: The request and sink text appears only inside a string; the actual sink receives a static literal.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant is present only as a comment in this negative control.
cases.whyFixed: The apparent flow exists only in a comment; the actual sink receives a static literal.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would use the shadowed request value as the sink argument.
cases.whyFixed: A nested parameter shadows the outer request name, while the HTML sink still receives a static literal.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would pass request command text to exec.
cases.whyFixed: The process command is fixed and does not use request input.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant appears only in the comment in this negative control.
cases.whyFixed: The apparent request command exists only in a comment; the actual command is static.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would replace the approved target with request URL input.
cases.whyFixed: The outbound request target is a fixed approved origin and path.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant appears only in the comment in this negative control.
cases.whyFixed: The apparent request URL appears only in a comment; the actual fetch target is static.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant would pass the unchecked request destination to redirect.

cases.whyVulnerable: The corresponding unsafe variant appears only in a string in this negative control.
cases.whyFixed: The request and redirect text appears only inside a string; the actual redirect is static.
